title: Partial Petrial Polynomials of Bouquets
summary: Gross, Mansour, and Tucker [European J. Combin., 95 (2021): 103329] introduced the \emph{partial Petrial polynomial} of a ribbon graph $G$, denoted by $^{\partial}{\varepsilon^{\times}_G}(z)$. For a prime bouquet $B_n$, Yan and Li [Discrete Appl. Math., 375 (2025): 281-289] determined $^{\partial}{\varepsilon^{\times}_{B_n}}(z)$ when the intersection graph $I(B_n)$ is either the complete graph or a path, and provided an equivalent condition under which the lowest degree of the nonzero coefficient in $^{\partial}{\varepsilon^{\times}_{B_n}}(z)$ is $1$.
